`nwsrfsr` wraps the legacy Fortran hydrology models from the National Weather
Service River Forecast System (NWSRFS) used operationally at the Northwest River
Forecast Center (NWRFC). You can run a complete basin configuration with one
call (`nwsrfs_run()` or `load_example()`), or compose the low-level wrappers
directly (`fa_nwrfc()`, `rsnwelev()`, `sac_snow()`, `uh()`, `lagk()`,
`chanloss()`, and `consuse()`).

## Model Chain Overview

In an NWRFC basin setup, 6-hour zone forcings pass through up to six stages:

1. **Forcing adjustments (`fa_nwrfc()`)**: Applies calibrated monthly
   climatological adjustments to mean areal precipitation (`map`), temperature
   (`mat`), rain/snow fraction (`ptps`), and potential evapotranspiration
   (`pet`), and computes evapotranspiration demand (`etd_mm`). Optionally,
   `rsnwelev()` derives `ptps` from a lapse rate and area-elevation curve.
2. **Snow and soil moisture (`sac_snow()`)**: Runs SNOW-17 and SAC-SMA on each
   elevation zone to produce total channel inflow (`tci`, mm per timestep).
3. **Unit hydrograph (`uh()`)**: Convolves per-zone `tci` with a two-parameter
   gamma unit hydrograph to produce local runoff in cubic feet per second (cfs).
4. **Upstream routing (`lagk()`)**: Routes upstream tributary inflows through
   variable Lag and K river reaches and adds them to local runoff.
5. **Channel loss/gain (`chanloss()`)**: Applies seasonal channel loss or gain
   factors above a minimum flow threshold.
6. **Consumptive use (`consuse()`)**: Computes daily irrigation diversions and
   return flows from a consumptive-use (`-CU`) zone and adjusts 6-hour flow.

## Running a Full Basin Simulation

`load_example()` runs the complete chain on either of the two bundled basins:

- **NRKW1** (Nooksack River at North Cedarville, WA; USGS 12210700): two
  SAC-SMA/SNOW-17 zones plus three upstream Lag-K tributaries (`MFNW1`,
  `NFNW1`, `NSSW1`).
- **SFLN2** (Salmon Falls Creek near San Jacinto, NV; USGS 13105000): two
  runoff zones plus a consumptive-use zone (`SFLN2-CU`) and seasonal channel
  losses.

```{r full-run}
library(nwsrfsr)

run_nrkw1 = load_example("NRKW1")
print(run_nrkw1)

run_sfln2 = load_example("SFLN2")
print(run_sfln2)
```

For external basins, point `nwsrfs_run()` at an NWRFC autocalibration directory
containing `forcing_por_*.csv`, `flow_daily_*.csv`, optional `upflow_*.csv`, and
a `results_*/pars_optimal.csv` parameter file (sample directories for five
basins are archived at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18829935>):

```r
run = nwsrfs_run("path/to/nwsrfs-ac-sample-runs/1zone/FSSO3")
```

### Plotting a Water Year Hydrograph

The returned `nwsrfs_run` list carries total simulated flow (`$sim`, cfs),
local runoff (`$sacsnow_sf`), routed upstream flow (`$lagk_route`), adjusted
forcings (`$forcings`), and the parameter table (`$pars`).

```{r plot-wy, fig.alt = "Simulated 6-hour streamflow at NRKW1 for water year 1996, decomposing total flow into local runoff and routed upstream tributaries."}
f1 = run_nrkw1$forcings[[1]]
dt = as.POSIXct(
  sprintf("%04d-%02d-%02d %02d:00:00", f1$year, f1$month, f1$day, f1$hour),
  tz = "UTC"
)
wy96 = dt >= as.POSIXct("1995-10-01", tz = "UTC") &
  dt < as.POSIXct("1996-10-01", tz = "UTC")

plot(
  dt[wy96],
  run_nrkw1$sim[wy96],
  type = "l",
  col = "#2b5c8f",
  lwd = 1.4,
  xlab = "Date (UTC)",
  ylab = "Discharge (cfs)",
  main = "NRKW1 Simulated Discharge (Water Year 1996)"
)
lines(dt[wy96], run_nrkw1$lagk_route[wy96], col = "#b35806", lwd = 1.1)
legend(
  "topright",
  legend = c("Total flow (local + Lag-K)", "Routed upstream (Lag-K)"),
  col = c("#2b5c8f", "#b35806"),
  lwd = c(1.4, 1.1),
  bty = "n"
)
```

### Controlling Forcing Adjustments and Flow Averaging

Both `nwsrfs_run()` and `load_example()` control climatological forcing
adjustments through `forcing_adj` (`TRUE`, `FALSE`, or a subset of `"map"`,
`"mat"`, `"ptps"`, and `"pet"`) and select between instantaneous and
period-average local runoff through `return_inst`:

```{r options}
run_unadj = load_example("NRKW1", forcing_adj = FALSE)
run_map_only = load_example("NRKW1", forcing_adj = "map", return_inst = FALSE)

c(
  adjusted_mean_cfs = mean(run_nrkw1$sim),
  unadjusted_mean_cfs = mean(run_unadj$sim),
  map_only_peravg_cfs = mean(run_map_only$sim)
)
```

## Updating Parameters

`update_pars()` replaces one or more parameter values by `p_name` and re-runs
the basin model while preserving the run options (`forcing_adj`, `shift_sf`, and
`return_inst`).

```{r update-pars}
# Inspect current upper-zone tension water capacity (uztwm, mm)
run_nrkw1$pars[run_nrkw1$pars$name == "uztwm", ]

# Increase zone 1 uztwm and re-run
new_pars = data.frame(p_name = "uztwm_NRKW1-1", value = 100.0)
run_updated = update_pars(run_nrkw1, new_pars)

c(baseline = mean(run_nrkw1$sim), updated = mean(run_updated$sim))
```

## Running Individual Components and Inspecting States

When building custom workflows or inspecting internal snow and soil moisture
states, call the component wrappers directly. Below we subset two water years of
NRKW1 inputs (`1980-10-01` through `1982-09-30`), compute adjusted forcings,
extract SNOW-17 and SAC-SMA states via `sac_snow_states()`, and route runoff:

```{r low-level, fig.alt = "Simulated snow water equivalent (SWE) for the lower and upper elevation zones of NRKW1 across two water years."}
dt_hours = 6L
keep = seq_len(2L * 365L * 4L)
forcing_sub = lapply(nrkw1_forcing, \(df) df[keep, ])
upflow_sub = lapply(nrkw1_upflow, \(df) df[keep, ])

# 1. Forcing adjustments + PET / ETD
forcing_adj = fa_nwrfc(dt_hours, forcing_sub, nrkw1_pars)

# 2. SNOW-17 and SAC-SMA with full state output
states = sac_snow_states(dt_hours, forcing_adj, nrkw1_pars)
tci = cbind(states$tci_1, states$tci_2)

# 3. Unit hydrograph + Lag-K routing
local_cfs = uh(dt_hours, tci, nrkw1_pars, sum_zones = TRUE)
routed_cfs = lagk(dt_hours, upflow_sub, nrkw1_pars, sum_routes = TRUE)
total_cfs = local_cfs + routed_cfs
head(total_cfs)

# Plot snow water equivalent (mm) across elevation zones
dt_sub = as.POSIXct(
  sprintf(
    "%04d-%02d-%02d %02d:00:00",
    states$year, states$month, states$day, states$hour
  ),
  tz = "UTC"
)
plot(
  dt_sub,
  states$swe_2,
  type = "l",
  col = "#2b5c8f",
  lwd = 1.4,
  xlab = "Date (UTC)",
  ylab = "SWE (mm)",
  main = "Simulated Snow Water Equivalent by Zone"
)
lines(dt_sub, states$swe_1, col = "#35978f", lwd = 1.2)
legend(
  "topright",
  legend = c("Zone 2 (upper)", "Zone 1 (lower)"),
  col = c("#2b5c8f", "#35978f"),
  lwd = c(1.4, 1.2),
  bty = "n"
)
```

### Rain-Snow Elevation (`rsnwelev()`)

When rain/snow partitioning is driven by an area-elevation curve rather than a
precomputed `ptps` column, `rsnwelev()` computes fractional snow area per
timestep from zone reference elevation (`elev`), temperature lapse rate (`talr`,
degC per 100 m), and rain/snow threshold temperature (`pxtemp`, degC):

```{r rsnwelev}
zones = c("SFLN2-1", "SFLN2-2")
sfln2_sub = lapply(sfln2_forcing[zones], \(df) df[1:40, ])

rs_pars = rbind(
  sfln2_pars[sfln2_pars$name == "elev" & sfln2_pars$zone %in% zones, ],
  data.frame(
    p_name = paste0(rep(c("talr_", "pxtemp_"), each = 2), zones),
    name = rep(c("talr", "pxtemp"), each = 2),
    type = "rsnwelev",
    zone = rep(zones, 2),
    value = c(0.55, 0.55, 1.0, 1.0)
  )
)

sfln2_ptps = rsnwelev(sfln2_sub, rs_pars, area_elev_curve)
summary(sfln2_ptps[["SFLN2-2"]]$ptps)
```

## Preprocessing Upstream Flow with `adjustq()`

`adjustq()` replicates the CHPS FEWS AdjustQ preprocessor: it snaps 6-hour
instantaneous observations to a regular grid, fills short and long observation
gaps using simulated discharge (when supplied), and iteratively scales 6-hour
flows to match observed mean daily volumes.

```{r adjustq}
# Subset calendar year 2010 of NRKW1 daily, instantaneous, and simulated flow
yr10_daily = nrkw1_daily_flow[nrkw1_daily_flow$year == 2010, ]
yr10_inst = nrkw1_inst_flow[nrkw1_inst_flow$year == 2010, ]
yr10_sim_idx = f1$year == 2010
yr10_sim = data.frame(
  f1[yr10_sim_idx, c("year", "month", "day", "hour")],
  flow_cfs = run_nrkw1$sim[yr10_sim_idx]
)

aq = adjustq(
  daily_flow = yr10_daily,
  inst_flow = yr10_inst,
  sim = yr10_sim
)
head(aq)
```
